extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural research community — grant applicants, program staff, and research administrators
extracted.subtask_description: A news-style collection of NIH policy updates, reminders, and resource announcements that affect preparing, submitting, and understanding NIH grant applications and awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting appropriate research models (including NAMs)
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators should select the models most appropriate for their specific research questions; NIH supports a wide range of scientifically sound approaches, including New Approach Methodologies (NAMs), to advance understanding of human health and disease.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasize human relevance and translational potential where appropriate; NAMs are supported but must be scientifically sound and fit the research question. Choose the model that best addresses the hypothesis/aims rather than adopting a method because it is novel or currently promoted.

rubrics_metrics.name: PF5 Collaborative International Research Projects — know the application format
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants for NIH’s Collaborative International Research Projects (PF5) should learn key features of the new award structure and application format, including how applications may be split into linked awards after review and before Just-in-Time requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Watch the NIH 6-minute overview video to understand PF5-specific formatting and the possibility that a single submission may be divided into multiple linked awards post-review; prepare application materials accordingly and anticipate potential splitting when planning budgets and project structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the 2026 Pilot Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plan format
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH issued a new 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format based on a simplified set of required elements to use when preparing Data Management and Sharing Plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing DMS plans for applicable submissions, use the new pilot format and include the simplified required elements specified by NIH. Consult the new resource for exact formatting and content requirements to avoid omission of required elements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embed replication and reproducibility across research and applications
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH’s Gold Standard Science plan and the Replication and Reproducibility Initiative encourage a culture that values replication and reproducibility; applicants should consider these priorities in applications, awards, and NIH-highlighted topics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address plans for replication, reproducibility, and methodological rigor in applications where relevant; align proposals with NIH expectations for reliability of biomedical research and include justification of replicability strategies, study design choices, and data-sharing practices that support reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand the meaning of 'Competitive But Not Discussed' review outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: Following emergency modifications to review processes after the lapse in appropriations, NIH designated the middle third of applications in a study section as 'competitive but not discussed,' recognizing that strong applications may fall below a 33% cut off.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If your application receives this designation, it means it was in the middle third and not selected for discussion; be aware this policy change affects how some meritorious applications are handled. Use available NIH resources to interpret score/status and consider resubmission strategies if warranted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prepare for centralized peer review under CSR
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH centralized all peer review within the Center for Scientific Review (CSR) to strengthen efficiency, competition, and transparency; applicants should be aware of changes to peer-review processes and study section handling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect potential changes to study section assignments, review logistics, and timing due to centralization. Monitor NIH communications about how centralization affects application triage, review criteria emphasis, and opportunities for applicants to respond to review outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small business applicants: NIH Seed Fund (Small Business Program) availability
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH’s Small Business Program (Seed Fund) is back, providing opportunities for innovators, founders, and R&D-driven small companies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Small business applicants and founders should review the reinstated program’s eligibility, scope, and application requirements; incorporate program-specific expectations (e.g., commercialization plan, milestones) when preparing proposals.
